entities.summary:
Metrodorus of Chios (Greek:Μήτροδorus Κοσιος) was a prominent Greek philosopher and one of the key figures associated with the development of Epicureanism.

Born in Chios, a Greek island in the Aegean Sea, Metrodorus studied under the tutelage of Democritus, a renowned philosopher who founded the school of Democritus. Metrodorus' teachings emphasized the importance of reason, individualism, and the pursuit of happiness.

Metrodorus' philosophical ideas were later adopted by Epicurus, who went on to found the Epicurean school in Athens. The Epicurean school became a major force in ancient Greek thought, influencing Western philosophy for centuries to come.

Metrodorus' legacy extends beyond his philosophical contributions. He was also a skilled writer and contributed to the development of ancient Greek literature.

The enduring impact of Metrodorus' ideas can be seen in the many philosophers and thinkers who followed in his footsteps, including Epicurus, Lucretius, and the Stoics.

Metrodorus' life was cut short when he died in 400 BCE, but his ideas continue to inspire and influence philosophers and scholars to this day.
